source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #283 (branch fix/277-f64-kernel-stack at head 46ac0aaeb6af667995d7e70089b5494f473b237c — branch commit f2ebe0e (restore tail dispatch in op_f64_const (#277)) plus merge commit 46ac0aa bringing in current main 057bb2a, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45189155375 and 45189167325 against the branch and pull-request run 45189083410, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #283 (#277, a long f64.const loop aborts the host with a stack overflow under the interpreter: the #240 identity barrier in op_f64_const passed the address of its function-local static to black_box, which materialises its argument in an address-taken stack slot, and that slot made LLVM drop the sibling call for the dispatch, so every execution left a live host frame behind — the f64-kernel aborted at n = 1,000,000 with the overflow threshold at n ≈ 258,683; the fix replaces the barrier in that one handler with a volatile load of the same static, which keeps the body distinct from op_i64_const but leaves no frame state, and the Op contract comment in common.rs now records the hazard; regression test f64_const_loop_keeps_direct_threading in tests/call_threading.rs). The branch merged current main (057bb2a, containing PRs #269, #273, #278, #275, #276, #280 and #281) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free (main does not touch numeric.rs, and the two sides' common.rs changes are in disjoint regions). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (057bb2a) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45189182011, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. 9 of the 32 gated series change: the release stripped file size grows by exactly +16 B in core, component, wasi, core-aot and wasi-threads (stripped .text unchanged there), and release-size component and wasi-threads shrink by exactly −16 B in both the stripped file and stripped .text sizes; the remaining 23 series are byte-identical. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.36% (1,169,031 B to 1,231,735 B), down from +5.37%. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
